column3: Copy three ConsoleApp zip packages from the network share to the Desktop, extract each, retarget its TargetFramework(s) to net10.0 (net10.0;net48 for the multi-targeted app) via Visual Studio, build, run, and validate output.

column4: Trigger
Resolve the current user's home directory into vars.home.
Open the Run dialog using Win + R
Enter the network share path.
Press Enter to open the share in File Explorer.
Locate the File Explorer window for the share; stash its hwnd.
Maximize the share Explorer window.

Activate the share Explorer window so its file list has keyboard focus (avoids clicking a hardcoded coordinate, which can land on one of this machine's many desktop shortcut tiles instead of empty space).
Type the filename to use Explorer's incremental type-ahead search (scrolls ConsoleApp1-80.zip into view and selects it, working around ListView virtualization on this large share folder).
Copy the selected file to the clipboard.
Close the share Explorer window now that the file is copied to the clipboard -- it is not needed again for this zip, and leaving it open would leak a stray File Explorer window per app.
Open the Run dialog using Win + R.

Maximize the Desktop Explorer window.

Force-navigate the address bar to shell:desktop, since reopening this window can sometimes land on Explorer's "Home" view instead of the actual Desktop folder (which would break the paste/type-ahead below).
Re-enter shell:desktop in the address bar.
Press Enter to confirm navigation to the Desktop folder.
Paste ConsoleApp1-80.zip onto the Desktop.
Tolerantly dismiss a 'Replace or Skip Files' conflict dialog if a same-named zip already exists on the Desktop from a prior run (no-op if the dialog does not appear).

Confirm ConsoleApp1-80.zip landed on the Desktop (via the Explorer file list, since this machine's Desktop is OneDrive-redirected to a non-portable path -- resolving that path is unnecessary when the same Explorer window can confirm the paste directly).
Select ConsoleApp1-80.zip on the Desktop using type-ahead search.
Locate the 'Extract all' command-bar button (shown when a .zip is selected).
Click 'Extract all'.
Locate the extraction wizard dialog; stash its hwnd.
Click Extract to unzip the file into the default destination folder.
Tolerantly dismiss a 'Replace or Skip Files' conflict dialog if the extracted folder already exists on the Desktop from a prior run (no-op if the dialog does not appear).
Wait for the ConsoleApp1-80 extraction dialog to close (extraction complete).
Re-activate the Desktop Explorer window.
Locate the extracted ConsoleApp1-80 folder by its exact name (avoids type-ahead ambiguity with the same-named .zip file still on the Desktop).
Click the ConsoleApp1-80 folder.
Open the ConsoleApp1-80 folder.
Select the ConsoleApp1 folder using type-ahead search.
Open the ConsoleApp1 folder.
Select ConsoleApp1.sln using type-ahead search.
Open ConsoleApp1.sln in Visual Studio.
Wait for Visual Studio to launch and load the solution; stash its pid/hwnd.
Maximize the Visual Studio window.

Close the 'Live Unit Testing' tool window if Visual Studio auto-opened it on solution load (observed live to sometimes dock over the editor; generic, tolerant no-op if it did not appear -- handles this globally for any solution instead of working around it per test case).
Wait for Solution Explorer to finish loading the project tree.
Locate the project node in Solution Explorer (exact name match, to avoid matching the solution root node which is named "Solution '<name>' (N of N projects)").
Right-click the project node.

Locate the Solution Explorer context menu popup (a dynamic-class WPF window with an empty title; filter by owning pid and approximate height to disambiguate from other same-pid empty-titled utility windows).
Locate the 'Edit Project File' menu item.
Click 'Edit Project File' to open the .csproj in the editor.
Locate the active ConsoleApp1.csproj text editor surface.

Click into the editor near its right edge (not its horizontal center) to place focus/caret -- a defensive margin in case any other tool window still occupies the left portion of the editor (the 'Live Unit Testing' auto-open case itself is now handled earlier, right after Visual Studio's window is found, via close_pane_if_present.py).
Open the in-editor Find and Replace panel.
Type the existing TargetFramework line into the Find field: <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
Tab to the Replace field.
Type the new TargetFramework line into the Replace field: <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
Press Enter to replace the match.
Close the Find and Replace panel.
Save the project file.
Build the solution (Ctrl+Shift+B).
Wait for the build to finish (status bar shows Build succeeded).
Run the app without debugging (Ctrl+F5).
Locate the Visual Studio Debug Console window running the app; stash its hwnd.
Validate the console output.
Take a screenshot of the result.
Close the Debug Console window.
Close Visual Studio.
